Sigil Decoding

This page records the current sigil-decoding and sigil-presentation policy for translated output in MAM with doc. It is a working document, not a claim that every sigil in the corpus is already fully decoded.

The shared source-and-evidence reference lives in MAM-basics/doc/sigil-decoding.md. This page captures the subset of that workstream that already affects presentation decisions in this published product. The tracking issue is issue 257. The public-documentation follow-up for cases where Wikisource is weak or missing is issue 259.

Workflow note: this page is manually maintained as a public-facing subset of the shared decoder reference. It is not generated automatically from sigil-decoding.md, so future edits should merge carefully with the current HTML instead of replacing it wholesale.

Current Presentation Policy

  • Keep sigils in Hebrew in translated prose by default.
  • Explain sigils rather than replacing them with a separate Latin-letter system.
  • Prefer true Hebrew gershayim, as in תנ״ך and כתי״ל, over ASCII quote substitutes.
  • Mark unresolved or conflicting decodings explicitly instead of flattening them into a false single meaning.
  • Support both a central-reference mode and a standalone-passage mode as future presentation options.

Why This Is Its Own Workstream

Sigil handling is not just a wording problem. It also needs a shared source of truth, explicit handling of uncertainty, and a display strategy that stays readable in English while still helping readers learn to parse the Hebrew note language itself.

ב2 The manuscript ת451 names: a Yemenite Ketuvim manuscript by Joseph ben Benaya, 1484–85, formerly Meir Benayahu Ms T 451 Confirmed Two sigils for one manuscript. MAM’s editor chose ב2 first, for its proximity to ב1, then abandoned it and switched to the number the manuscript had when Meir Benayahu held it, without updating the uses already written. The corpus was repointed on 2026-08-27, in 32 places over six chapters of Daniel, so MAM as it now stands has no ב2. Older text still has it — Wikisource page history, and the Sefaria and Accordance derivatives until each refreshes — which is why this row stays. This page said until 2026-08-27 that local evidence leaned against the identification; that inference was drawn carefully from real evidence and the editor’s account overturned it.

How a Qualifier Applies to a Sigil List

A qualifier names the kind of evidence a sigil cites. For example, מסורת names a note in a source's masorah, and מסורות names notes in the masorah of two or more sources. Comma-joined lists under these two qualifiers distribute over the list: each listed source is cited for its masorah, as the editor confirms in his first reply.

Other qualifiers do not follow one uniform rule. In his answer to five worked examples, MAM's editor identifies both shared qualifiers and lists containing different kinds of evidence. The clauses below are those quoted in the question; several source notes have since been revised.

Clause quoted in the questionSiteSupported reading
ל,ב1,ש2-כתיב Daniel 3:5 The ketiv is in all three manuscripts: 3 ketiv attestations.
ל,ל1,ש,ש1,ק3,ו,ל3,ל9-כתיב Deuteronomy 28:30 The pointed ketiv is written thus in all eight manuscripts: 8 ketiv attestations.
במ"ק-ב,ק13 Genesis 43:26 The masorah qetannah in both manuscripts has the cited note: 2 masorah attestations.
ק3,ל-קטנות Deuteronomy 32:18 The text of ק3 supplies the reading; the small-letter list at the back of the Leningrad Codex supplies the list evidence: 1 small-letter-list attestation, on ל.
א,ל,ש1,ק-מ,ל-גדולות Psalms 84:4 The four manuscript texts lack the large ק, but the large-letter list of ל has it. The old note was mistaken: 1 large-letter-list attestation supports the large letter, while the four manuscript-text readings support its absence.

The current notes for Daniel 3:5 and Deuteronomy 28:30 retain their lists but identify the ketiv in prose rather than a trailing -כתיב. Psalms 84:4 now separates ל-גדולות,קורן supporting the large letter from א,ל,ש1,ק-מ supporting its absence.

These local counts do not replace the dated qualifier-table totals in the shared reference. A rule for every occurrence of the other qualifiers remains unresolved, as do the question's longhand-equivalence and sentence-comma controls. Historical increments cannot simply be added to a current count of hyphenated compounds when the source clauses have changed.

At Genesis 43:28, the local ketiv explanation still has ל,לו,ק3=, beside ל,ל1,ק3= in the qere explanation. The editor's later clarification, rewrite, and final-touch comments do not explicitly decode לו as ל1 or ל,ו. That spelling remains unresolved here.

Two Presentation Modes To Support

Central-reference mode. Leave sigils in Hebrew and link them to a central decoder, optionally with hover text or tooltips.

Standalone passage mode. Leave sigils in Hebrew in the translated prose, but append a compact decoder table containing only the sigils used in that passage.

These modes are compatible. A central decoder can coexist with smaller passage-local decoder tables.

Near-Term Work

  • Use the corpus inventory in MAM-basics to prioritize real sigils instead of guessed ones.
  • Continue promoting mature entries from issue 259 when the public note can state the evidence cleanly.
  • Feed confirmed and clearly-labeled provisional decisions into future translated-note output in this product.

This page is intentionally conservative. When in doubt, preserve uncertainty and link back to the shared evidence trail rather than guessing.
